models.title: Signed point price elasticity from a local response derivative
models.summary: Dimensionless local relative response of a positive demanded or supplied quantity to a positive price, preserving derivative sign. A supplied derivative is an input, not an estimated parameter or a finite-change forecast.

relationship.original_equation: Signed elasticity = (P/Q)(dQ/dP), applying source generic x/y dy/dx with x=P, y=Q; source demand magnitude epsilon = -(P/Q)dQ/dP.
relationship.locator: Leibniz 7.8.1, 'Elasticity in general' and calculus definition above the examples
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced s is the local partial derivative dQ/dP with other determinants fixed; no differentiation operator is executed. e is signed, so e=-epsilon for the source's downward-demand magnitude convention. Generic source definition supports either derivative sign; no claim that every curve is demand. Dimensional check: [unit/(currency/unit)]*[currency/unit]/[unit]=1. Unit is a declared homogeneous good/service unit over a fixed observation interval, not an arbitrary mix. Infinitesimal definition requires P>0 as well as Q>0 even though P appears in a numerator after simplification.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced s = dQ/dP in source generic definition
variables.definition: Local derivative of the selected demanded or supplied quantity with respect to its own price, holding non-price determinants fixed.
variables.context: Same good/service, population/market, demand or supply curve, observation interval and price basis at one operating point; all non-price determinants held fixed. P and Q must lie on that same differentiable response curve.
variables.domain: Finite signed derivative, including zero; independently supplied for this point; not a secant slope.

variables.source_symbol: P; x in the generic final subsection
variables.definition: Positive price per homogeneous unit, on the declared monetary/quality basis.
variables.context: Same good/service, population/market, demand or supply curve, observation interval and price basis at one operating point; all non-price determinants held fixed. P and Q must lie on that same differentiable response curve.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive; same currency scale and nominal/real basis used in s.

variables.source_symbol: Q; y in the generic final subsection
variables.definition: Positive demanded or supplied physical quantity for the declared observation interval at P.
variables.context: Same good/service, population/market, demand or supply curve, observation interval and price basis at one operating point; all non-price determinants held fixed. P and Q must lie on that same differentiable response curve.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive quantity at that curve point.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced e = signed generic elasticity; negative of source demand epsilon
variables.definition: Signed ratio of infinitesimal relative quantity change to relative own-price change.
variables.context: Same good/service, population/market, demand or supply curve, observation interval and price basis at one operating point; all non-price determinants held fixed. P and Q must lie on that same differentiable response curve.
variables.domain: Finite signed; negative for negative derivative; zero for locally flat response.

assumptions: Source assumption: positive differentiable response, evaluated at a single point.
Application context: when interpreting demand or supply, keep non-price determinants, population and observation interval fixed; no causal effect is identified from two arbitrary observations.
limitations: Does not compute the derivative, estimate elasticity, predict demand or assert equilibrium.
Point and arc elasticities differ; a local derivative does not establish constant elasticity over a finite interval.

sources.title: The CORE Team, The Economy 1.0, Leibniz 7.8.1: The elasticity of demand
sources.version: Version 1.14.1; copyright CORE Economics Education 2022, verified on copyright page
sources.locator: Calculus definition; Beautiful Cars linear example; final subsection 'Elasticity in general'
sources.evidence: Defines signed generic elasticity as x/y times dy/dx for positive differentiable response; price-demand presentation uses its negative. Linear car example reports magnitude 49 at P=7840, Q=2 and 0.053 at P=400, Q=95.

references.method: Published result with explicit sign-convention conversion: source demand magnitude 49 becomes signed -49. Source inverse curve P=8000-80Q gives dQ/dP=-1/80. Tolerance covers floating arithmetic only.
references.provenance: https://books.core-econ.org/the-economy-v1/book/text/leibniz-07-08-01.html, linear Beautiful Cars example, price 7840 and quantity 2.

references.method: Published rounded magnitude 0.053 converted to signed -0.053; half of 0.001 rounding unit bounds exact -1/19. Source input values are exact teaching data.
Limiting identity: no local quantity response gives zero relative response despite nonzero price/quantity.
references.provenance: Curator synthetic boundary, not observed economic data.

rejection_cases.reason: Relative price change has a zero base; simplification must not admit P=0.
Relative quantity change has a zero base.
Missing local derivative; observations alone do not supply it.

models.inverse_notes: Solve s=eQ/P given e,Q,P with P,Q>0; unique finite signed s. Substitution: e=-49,Q=2,P=7840 gives s=-0.0125 and forward -49. With s nonzero, P=eQ/s (require P>0) and Q=sP/e (require e nonzero,Q>0) are algebraic port solutions only. At s=e=0 every positive P,Q is compatible; e=0 with s nonzero is incompatible for positive P,Q. Positive P,Q do not guarantee a solved port lies on a supplied economic curve. No derivative, causal or statistical inverse is inferred.

gaps: New quantity meanings signed_point_price_elasticity, quantity_price_derivative, unit_price and economic_quantity; good-unit and price/derivative unit support and explicit curve contexts required. Runtime does not calculate derivatives.

models.title: Signed midpoint arc price elasticity
models.summary: Finite-interval ratio of midpoint-relative quantity and price changes. Symmetric between endpoints, preserving the sign; distinct from derivative-based point elasticity.

relationship.locator: Section 5.1, Midpoint Method equations and sign convention before 'Calculating Price Elasticity of Demand'
relationship.translation_notes: Source percentage factors 100 cancel. Literal 2 is arithmetic mean divisor, not a physical coefficient. Preserve midpoint denominators and nonzero price difference. P endpoints are strictly positive to retain positive-price economic profile; quantities may include one zero endpoint if their average is positive. Dimensional check: (U/U)/[(currency/U)/(currency/U)]=1. e_arc is introduced signed ratio, rather than the textbook's absolute reported demand magnitude. Not an instruction to extrapolate from the finite interval.

variables.source_symbol: P1
variables.definition: Price per homogeneous unit at endpoint 1.
variables.context: Same homogeneous good/service, price and quantity units, demand or supply schedule, population, price basis and observation interval at both endpoints; hold other determinants fixed for curve interpretation. Endpoints may be relabeled without changing the ratio.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive.

variables.source_symbol: P2
variables.definition: Price per homogeneous unit at endpoint 2.
variables.context: Same homogeneous good/service, price and quantity units, demand or supply schedule, population, price basis and observation interval at both endpoints; hold other determinants fixed for curve interpretation. Endpoints may be relabeled without changing the ratio.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive.

variables.source_symbol: Q1
variables.definition: Demanded or supplied quantity for the fixed observation interval at endpoint 1.
variables.context: Same homogeneous good/service, price and quantity units, demand or supply schedule, population, price basis and observation interval at both endpoints; hold other determinants fixed for curve interpretation. Endpoints may be relabeled without changing the ratio.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; both quantities cannot be zero.

variables.source_symbol: Q2
variables.definition: Demanded or supplied quantity for the fixed observation interval at endpoint 2.
variables.context: Same homogeneous good/service, price and quantity units, demand or supply schedule, population, price basis and observation interval at both endpoints; hold other determinants fixed for curve interpretation. Endpoints may be relabeled without changing the ratio.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; both quantities cannot be zero.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced e_arc: signed ratio of source midpoint percentage changes
variables.definition: Signed relative quantity change divided by relative price change using midpoint bases.
variables.context: Same homogeneous good/service, price and quantity units, demand or supply schedule, population, price basis and observation interval at both endpoints; hold other determinants fixed for curve interpretation. Endpoints may be relabeled without changing the ratio.
variables.domain: Finite signed, including zero for unchanged quantity with changed price.

constants.meaning: Arithmetic divisor defining each two-endpoint mean

assumptions: Source assumption: midpoint bases describe the same demand or supply curve interval.
Application context: all non-price determinants and the quantity observation window must be held fixed for an own-price elasticity interpretation.
limitations: Two observations from shifting curves do not identify a causal elasticity.
No constant elasticity, forecast or exact derivative at either endpoint is implied.

sources.title: Greenlaw, Shapiro and MacDonald, Principles of Economics 3e, section 5.1
sources.locator: Midpoint Method equations; Figure 5.2 B-to-A and Work It Out G-to-H; sign discussion
sources.evidence: Uses midpoint averages as both percentage bases. Published demand examples give magnitudes 0.45 and 1.47 and explicitly suppress negative signs. Source also applies the definition to supply; response signs are retained here.

references.method: Published magnitude 0.45 converted to -0.45 under the signed convention. Exact midpoint result -0.44827586 differs by less than half a hundredth; rounded intermediate percentages are not treated as exact.
Published magnitude 1.47 converted to -1.47, tolerance half a hundredth. Exact ratio -25/17 is within this rounding bound.
Independent limiting identity: unchanged quantity has zero relative change, while midpoint price change is nonzero.

rejection_cases.reason: No price change; ratio denominator zero.
Zero mean quantity makes the relative change undefined.
Selected positive-price profile excludes a zero endpoint.

models.inverse_notes: Given e_arc,P1,P2,Q1, set k=e_arc*(P2-P1)/(P2+P1). Then Q2=Q1*(1+k)/(1-k), provided 1-k is nonzero and all original guards, Q2>=0 and Q1+Q2>0 hold. Example e_arc=-1, P1=10,P2=20,Q1=20 yields k=-1/3,Q2=10, whose midpoint changes are -2/3 and 2/3, giving -1. At k=1 with Q1>0 no finite Q2 exists; with Q1=0, any Q2>0 gives k=1, so ambiguous. e_arc=0 with distinct positive prices and Q1>0 uniquely gives Q2=Q1. Endpoint reversal preserves both signs and their ratio (B-to-A reversed also -0.44827586). Other inverse targets not formally enumerated or tested.

gaps: New signed_arc_price_elasticity and economic price/quantity meanings and units; economic context matching is needed. No projection into discount_rate.

models.title: Current-price GDP expenditure identity
models.summary: Accounting total of final expenditures on domestic production. Private investment includes fixed investment plus inventory change; imported production is removed once. This is an identity, with no behavioral response or equilibrium assertion.

relationship.original_equation: GDP = PCE + gross private domestic fixed investment + change in private inventories + government consumption expenditures and gross investment + exports - imports.
relationship.locator: Chapter 2, printed pp. 2-8 to 2-9 (PDF pages 8-9), 'As the sum of goods and services sold to final users'
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced I groups gross private fixed investment and change in private inventories; C=PCE, G=government consumption plus gross investment, X=exports, M=positive-signed import amount. Each is a current-price flow over the same accounting interval; no stock of capital or securities enters. Dimensional check: currency+currency+currency+currency-currency=currency. Do not sum separately chain-weighted real components. Data revisions/rounding can prevent observed published tables from balancing exactly; this relationship defines the accounting total at a consistent vintage, not the equality of independent GDP and GDI estimates.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced C maps to source PCE
variables.definition: Current-price personal consumption expenditures by or on behalf of persons under NIPA scope.
variables.context: Same national economy under BEA NIPA expenditure definitions, accounting interval, data vintage, current-price USD scale and seasonal/annual-rate convention for every component; amounts are interval flows, or consistently reported annual-rate flow levels.
variables.domain: Finite amount; usually nonnegative; no scalar sign restriction is needed for the accounting identity.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced I = source gross private fixed investment + change in private inventories
variables.definition: Current-price private fixed capital formation plus inventory change, before depreciation; excludes purchases of financial securities.
variables.context: Same national economy under BEA NIPA expenditure definitions, accounting interval, data vintage, current-price USD scale and seasonal/annual-rate convention for every component; amounts are interval flows, or consistently reported annual-rate flow levels.
variables.domain: Finite signed; inventory liquidation can offset fixed investment, so do not impose I>=0.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced G maps to source government consumption expenditures and gross investment
variables.definition: Current-price consumption expenditures and gross fixed investment of government under NIPA scope; excludes transfers as such.
variables.context: Same national economy under BEA NIPA expenditure definitions, accounting interval, data vintage, current-price USD scale and seasonal/annual-rate convention for every component; amounts are interval flows, or consistently reported annual-rate flow levels.
variables.domain: Finite amount; requires correct source accounting classification.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced X maps to source exports
variables.definition: Value of goods and services transferred by residents to foreign residents during the matching interval.
variables.context: Same national economy under BEA NIPA expenditure definitions, accounting interval, data vintage, current-price USD scale and seasonal/annual-rate convention for every component; amounts are interval flows, or consistently reported annual-rate flow levels.
variables.domain: Finite on source sign convention, with exports entered additively.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced M maps to source imports
variables.definition: Value of goods and services transferred by foreign residents to residents; supplied as an amount before subtraction.
variables.context: Same national economy under BEA NIPA expenditure definitions, accounting interval, data vintage, current-price USD scale and seasonal/annual-rate convention for every component; amounts are interval flows, or consistently reported annual-rate flow levels.
variables.domain: Finite import amount on the positive-import convention, not already negated.

variables.source_symbol: GDP
variables.definition: Current-price value of domestic final production over the specified interval as measured by expenditure categories.
variables.context: Same national economy under BEA NIPA expenditure definitions, accounting interval, data vintage, current-price USD scale and seasonal/annual-rate convention for every component; amounts are interval flows, or consistently reported annual-rate flow levels.
variables.domain: Finite accounting sum; no extrapolation from nominal to real output.

assumptions: Source accounting convention: components exhaust and partition final expenditure categories, with foreign production offset by imports.
Application scope: use current-price values with matching vintage, interval and accounting conventions; retain imputed/nonmarket transactions required by NIPA.
limitations: Not valid for summing independently chained-dollar real GDP components.
Classification, data collection and adjustment are external inputs; this arithmetic does not establish that supplied values conform to NIPA definitions or estimate a causal import effect.

references.method: Independent production-side construction: domestic intermediate producer adds 35, final producer adds 100, so total value added is 135. Complete final-use ledger assigns domestic consumption 75 plus imported consumption 15, domestic investment 30, government 20 and exports 10. No other imports, inventory or flows. Checks expenditure against production-side value added, not another ordering of the same five-term sum.
references.provenance: Curator synthetic balanced transaction ledger using BEA chapter 2 expenditure and value-added concepts; no observed national data.

references.method: Independent stock/production ledger: domestic new production is 80 (60 sold to consumers and 20 to government); consumption additionally draws 10 of previously produced inventory, giving C=70 and inventory investment -10. Current production remains 80. This tests a signed investment flow rather than imposing positive I.
references.provenance: Curator synthetic current-period production and inventory ledger; source conceptual support BEA chapter 2 pp. 2-8 to 2-9.

rejection_cases.reason: Missing imports cannot silently be assumed zero.

models.inverse_notes: Each additive component is uniquely recoverable from GDP and all four other components under the same measurement conventions: C=GDP-I-G-X+M; I=GDP-C-G-X+M; G=GDP-C-I-X+M; X=GDP-C-I-G+M; M=C+I+G+X-GDP. No denominator exclusions or multiple branches. Substitution in ordinary ledger gives M=90+30+20+10-135=15 and forward GDP=135. All-zero flows give GDP=0 and uniquely zero missing component when other values are known. Missing two or more components is underdetermined; algebra does not identify behavioral/counterfactual changes.

gaps: New national-accounting meanings required even though USD exists. Metadata must bind accounting period, vintage and current-price conventions; amounts must not be relabeled operating_cost.

models.title: Annualized geometric growth from dated endpoints
models.summary: Descriptive annualized compound rate connecting two positive levels over n equal observation periods, m periods per year. Annual data m=1 gives CAGR. Intermediate volatility and future growth are not inferred.

relationship.locator: Chapter 4, printed p. 4-29 (PDF page 29), Growth rates; corroborated BEA FAQ 463
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced Yt,Y0 generalize GDP_t,GDP_0 to the same positive NIPA economic activity series. g is fractional per-annum growth, so BEA's percent factor 100 is removed. Literal 1 is identity growth factor. Ratio is dimensionless; exponent m/n is elapsed years reciprocal using numeric period counts; output is 1 as a fractional effective annual rate. Annual case m=1 uses n elapsed year intervals (not n endpoint observations). Positive endpoints choose the unique positive real gross-growth factor; no logarithm execution. PDF text and official indexed equation inspected; screenshot calls returned an image marker without usable image pixels in this host, so no visual inspection is claimed.

variables.definition: Earlier positive level of the same economic activity series; date recorded in context.
variables.context: Same positive economic series, geography/population, quantity definition, monetary/price basis and revision vintage at both dated endpoints; n is elapsed equal observation intervals, m is intervals per year, both on the same calendar convention.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive level on fixed nominal or real basis; the formula also applies to other units only after separately declaring compatible ports.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced Yt = GDP_t or corresponding activity level
variables.definition: Later positive level of the same economic activity series; same currency and price basis as Y0.
variables.context: Same positive economic series, geography/population, quantity definition, monetary/price basis and revision vintage at both dated endpoints; n is elapsed equal observation intervals, m is intervals per year, both on the same calendar convention.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive; zero or negative economic balances are outside this compound positive-series profile.

variables.source_symbol: m
variables.definition: Number of equal observation intervals per calendar year; annual=1, quarterly=4, monthly=12 where that observation convention applies.
variables.context: Same positive economic series, geography/population, quantity definition, monetary/price basis and revision vintage at both dated endpoints; n is elapsed equal observation intervals, m is intervals per year, both on the same calendar convention.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive; convention supplied, not estimated and not a time-series observation count.

variables.source_symbol: n
variables.definition: Number of equal elapsed observation intervals from earlier date to later date.
variables.context: Same positive economic series, geography/population, quantity definition, monetary/price basis and revision vintage at both dated endpoints; n is elapsed equal observation intervals, m is intervals per year, both on the same calendar convention.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive integer for regularly spaced period observations; date/frequency consistency checked externally. Positive noninteger intervals require a declared prorating convention.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced g = BEA r/100
variables.definition: Fractional annual compound rate matching the two endpoint levels.
variables.context: Same positive economic series, geography/population, quantity definition, monetary/price basis and revision vintage at both dated endpoints; n is elapsed equal observation intervals, m is intervals per year, both on the same calendar convention.
variables.domain: Finite greater than -1, including zero or negative contraction.

constants.meaning: Unit gross-growth factor subtracted to obtain net fractional rate

assumptions: Source convention: n counts elapsed data periods and m is periodicity per year.

Application profile: positive endpoint levels, compatible series definitions and fixed currency/price basis. Constancy is an equivalent rate representation, not an assumption that each historical interval actually grew at this rate.
limitations: Endpoint-only statistic ignores the intermediate path and does not forecast.
Nominal and real growth describe different series. Do not mix current dollars with chained dollars or use arbitrary positive ratios to claim real growth.
Numerical evaluator bounds exponent magnitude at 100; extremely short fractional intervals may need another runtime. Scientific profile itself is not restricted to this machine limit.

references.method: Published 21.6 percent normalized to expected 0.216, without replacing it by exact 0.21550625. Tolerance 0.0005 corresponds to half of 0.1 percentage point source rounding unit.
Independent forward path: 200 -> 220 -> 242 -> 266.2 consists of three exact 10-percent increases. Thus endpoint annual equivalent is 0.1; tolerance handles floating cube-root rounding.
references.provenance: Curator constructed three annual intervals; not a published data estimate.

references.method: Limiting identity: identical positive endpoints imply unit gross factor and zero equivalent growth over seven elapsed years.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero initial level does not define a ratio.
No positive elapsed time; annualized exponent undefined.
Negative endpoint excluded by positive compound-series definition.

models.inverse_notes: Solve Yt=Y0*(1+g)**(n/m) or Y0=Yt/(1+g)**(n/m) with g>-1 and m,n>0, retaining positive levels. Synthetic check g=.1,Y0=200,n=3,m=1 yields 266.2; forward gives .1. At g=0, Yt=Y0 for every positive elapsed count, so n or m cannot be identified. For unequal endpoints, an inverse n would require logarithms and g nonzero with positive compatible logarithm signs; that direction is not provided or tested. No negative real gross-growth branch admitted. Machine exponent limits apply separately from scientific admissibility.

gaps: New economic_series_level, annualized_geometric_growth_rate and periods_per_year meanings required; period_count is reusable from snapshot. Runtime needs dimensionless ratio powers with input-dependent exponents; no projection supplied.
